newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends mostly down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Tuesday, with market sentiment remaining poor, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,311 yuan ($398) per tonne, losing four yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 3,338 and hit a low of 3,310.
January fell 17 to 3,220 yuan, March 36 to 3,212, May unchanged at 3,246, July dropped 30 to 3,320 and September 15 to 3,345.
Combined volume fell sharply to 8,900 tonnes from 85,800.
Traders said many investors stayed on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news. "Profit-taking by retail investors caused today's falls," one trader said.
"A surplus of spot soybean limits the potential for further rises," a second trader said.
